title: Encoding a decoded circle code returns the original integer
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 591-594 (book Lemma 8.1.8): for every point x of the circle and every element c of its code, encoding the decode of c returns c. The statement is an identity between composites and gives no computation, and the proof (source lines 596-623) has to run a circle induction whose loop case is dismissed only because the integers are a set, then reduce the base case to an arithmetic identity about loop powers, which is settled by induction on the integers with a successor step that unwinds the definition of the loop powers, the definition of encode, functoriality of transport and the transport computation along the generating loop. Which of these four rewrites supplies which factor of the final arithmetic is exactly the content, and none of it is visible in the statement.
